text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Leaders of Bulgarian political parties represented in parliament signed an anti-crisis declaration and gave support to President Petar Stoyanov's demand for wider powers of a caretaker government.

-- Bulgaria's outgoing Socialists agreed to give a caretaker cabinet extended powers to negotiate and conclude agreements with international financial institution to ease the country's severe economic crisis.
-- President Petar Stoyanov is expected to name today a caretaker government under Sofia mayor Stefan Sofianski to govern until after early general elections in mid-April.
-- Parliament will debate today amendments to the electoral law and is expected to give extended powers to a caretaker cabinet.

-- Socialist deputies would insist on lowering the barrier for entering parliament in the forthcoming early elections to three percent of the vote from four percent, the Socialist parliamentary group decided.
-- Two workers were killed and two were injured by a gas leak at Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftohim, the refinery said.
-- Passenger railway fares are expected to rise by 50 percent from March 1 after a 39 percent rise from February 1 under a proposal by railways experts.
-- Prices of basic goods monitored by the cabinet rose by 134 percent on the average in the past ten days, the National Statistics Institute said.
